diagnosis.root_cause: The ONU optical path changed from a stable 95 km to 41 km, indicating a fibre-route, splice, patching, or splitter-path change. After that step change, RX power progressively degraded from approximately -18 dBm to -26.6 dBm while TX power and TX bias remained normal. This is causing degraded optical service and likely signal-related session instability.
evidence: The ONU is online and responding, so this is not an ONU-offline fault.
The 168-hour distance telemetry is constant at 95 km, then makes a discrete step to 41 km and remains there; distance is expected to be constant, so this indicates a changed fibre path.
RX power was initially around -21 dBm, briefly improved to about -18 dBm at the distance step, then steadily deteriorated to -26.4 to -26.6 dBm, which is in the degraded range.
Live ONU RX is -26.58 dBm, confirming the degraded optical condition.
TX power is approximately +2.4 dBm and TX bias current remains around 11 mA, so there is no evidence of laser degradation or an ONU transmitter fault.
Other ONUs on EPON0/5 have generally normal RX levels, and all tested ONUs are online, arguing against a PON-port failure or broad splitter failure.
The OLT is healthy with normal CPU, memory, temperature, uptime, ping, SNMP, and PON status, ruling out an OLT fault.
The customer has 8 sessions in 24 hours with short average duration, exceeding the flapping threshold; this is consistent with the degraded optical path but is not the primary fault.
VLAN 1115, RADIUS records, assigned IP, router heartbeat, and authentication consistency are normal, ruling out provisioning, router, and RADIUS faults.

remediation.action: Escalate for physical fibre-path investigation. Compare the current route with the intended 95 km path, inspect and clean ONU/ODF/splitter connectors, verify patching and splitter assignment, and perform OTDR and optical-loss tests. Restore the correct fibre path or repair the affected splice/section. Recheck RX power, distance, and session stability after repair.

ground_truth.root_cause: A re-splice four days ago shortened the path from 95 m to 41 m and initially improved RX from -20.8 to -18.2 dBm. Since then RX has fallen steadily to -26.5 dBm, so the new splice itself is failing.
expected_reasoning: Current RX of -26.1 dBm is in the degraded band and live RX is worse still at -26.6
The recent RX series shows a clear downward slope, which alone reads as fibre degradation
Looking further back, distance stepped from 95 m to 41 m four days ago
At that same moment RX jumped upward from -20.8 to -18.2 dBm, consistent with a shorter path
So the sequence is: path shortened and improved first, then began degrading from the new baseline
The customer's statement that it was fixed last week corroborates a work visit at that point
TX power, bias current and supply voltage are flat, so the ONU is not implicated
Peers on EPON0/5 are normal, so the fault is in this customer's own path
A splice made four days ago that is now losing 8 dB is a defective splice, not coincidental degradation

expected_escalation.review_reason: Rework of a splice completed four days ago; the original job should be reviewed

distractors: The recent RX slope is a textbook fibre degradation signature
The distance step is buried three days back in the series
Eight sessions in 24h invites a flapping diagnosis
